dish: New Orleans Red Beans and Rice
notes: Low and slow — plan for 5-6 hours total cook time.

ingredients: 1/2 stick unsalted butter plus one more pad
steps: Soak the beans in water overnight in the fridge.
Dice all produce — bell peppers, onion, and parsley.
Slice tasso and andouille into bite-size chunks.
Melt half a stick of butter and 1 tbsp avocado oil in a big pot.
Add sausage and tasso to the pot. Brown for a few minutes, stirring to get all sides.
After a few minutes, add all the diced produce.
Add 4 good back-and-forth shakes of Tony's, garlic powder, and onion powder. Add 2 good shakes of Italian seasoning and 1 good shake of thyme. Add 5 bay leaves.
When produce is translucent, add soaked beans, 32 oz chicken broth, ham hocks, and enough water to fully cover and make it a bit soupy.
Bring to a boil, then slowly reduce to a simmer.
Simmer with the lid on but slightly cracked for ventilation. Stir every 20-30 minutes so it doesn't stick.
After about 4-5 hours, remove ham hocks and mash some beans in the pot to thicken.
Add a pad of butter. Continue simmering for another hour or two.
After mashing and thickening, turn heat down to low (1-2). Beans can stick/burn easily once thick.
Serve over rice with green onion and any other fixings.
